derivation_notes: For a nonconserved scalar order parameter, curvature-driven interface motion has a characteristic velocity proportional to interface mobility times interfacial tension times curvature. Dynamic scaling gives curvature of order 1/L, yielding dL/dt = interface_mobility * interfacial_tension / L, which is nonnegative and decreases as L grows for positive parameters.

states.description: Characteristic domain length in fixed microscopic length units

scenario_text: Consider phase ordering after a rapid quench of a solid with a nonconserved scalar structural order parameter into a two-phase coexistence region. Curved interfaces move to reduce interfacial free energy, causing a characteristic domain length to grow with time. Evolve that length from an initial microstructure while mobility and interfacial tension are held fixed. The target is the instantaneous coarsening rate generated by curvature-driven interface motion.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.interface_mobility: positive initial value; typically greater than or equal to minimum_interface_mobility
new_symbol_range_suggestions.mobility_relaxation_time: positive; typically comparable to or larger than the early coarsening time
new_symbol_range_suggestions.minimum_interface_mobility: nonnegative and not exceeding the initial interface_mobility

derivation_notes: Retaining curvature-driven capillary motion but promoting interface_mobility to a relaxing state gives dL_dt = interface_mobility*interfacial_tension/L with a saturating aging law d(interface_mobility)/dt = -(interface_mobility - minimum_interface_mobility)/mobility_relaxation_time. The initial condition interface_mobility = 1.0 preserves the parent experiment at t = 0 while remaining non-degenerate when minimum_interface_mobility < 1.0; if initialized exactly at the floor, the added state lies on a zero-evolution set and the parent law is recovered.
change_summary: The constant-mobility assumption is relaxed to allow time-dependent mobility aging toward a finite residual floor, modeling defect-drag or structural-relaxation slowdown during coarsening. This changes the scored target mapping because dL_dt now depends on the evolving kinetic state, producing extra late-time suppression beyond a single fixed-gain 1/L law.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Interface mobility is strictly constant throughout coarsening.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Time-dependent interface mobility due to evolving defect drag or structural relaxation during coarsening.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: If mobility_relaxation_time -> oo, or if interface_mobility is initialized at a constant stationary value with zero RHS such as interface_mobility = minimum_interface_mobility, then interface_mobility remains constant and the parent law is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: With constant interface_mobility and interfacial_tension, the target mapping is dL_dt = interface_mobility*interfacial_tension/L, so the coarsening rate is a single 1/L decay with one shared gain over all times.
response_change.child_relation: Release the assumption of permanently constant interface_mobility by allowing mobility to evolve downward during aging, so dL_dt remains proportional to 1/L but with a time-history-dependent prefactor set by a relaxing mobility state.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories observed over longer times from the same initial L, the child predicts an additional slowdown beyond the parent’s fixed-gain 1/L law; late-time rates are lower than early-time rates at the same L-scale progression, while the parent can only rescale the whole curve uniformly.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the interface kinetics age on the same order as the coarsening time, so mobility relaxation is not negligible over the measured time window; if mobility remains effectively constant, the parent law is recovered.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training over moderate times the mechanism appears as mild sub-Lifshitz slowdown; in holdout at longer times the same mobility-aging process produces stronger late-time suppression of dL_dt, extending the same trend rather than introducing a new regime.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Take the mobility-relaxation timescale to infinity, or initialize the mobility state at its stationary constant value with no evolution, to recover dL_dt = interface_mobility*interfacial_tension/L exactly.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A genuine aging slowdown requires memory of elapsed evolution, not just the instantaneous state L. With only L present, any admissible deterministic target remains a function of L alone and cannot represent history-dependent kinetic prefactor relaxation.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: mobility aging with a finite residual kinetic floor
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Time-dependent interface mobility due to evolving defect drag or structural relaxation during coarsening.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement is structurally harder because the target now depends on a hidden relaxing state with a finite saturation level, creating a history-dependent asymptotic slowdown that cannot be mimicked by any coefficient-only rescaling of the parent 1/L law.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Interface mobility and interfacial tension are constant.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Interfacial tension remains constant but interface mobility ages dynamically toward a finite residual value during coarsening.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: If mobility_relaxation_time -> oo, or if interface_mobility is initialized at a constant stationary value with zero RHS such as interface_mobility = minimum_interface_mobility, then interface_mobility remains constant and the parent law is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: dL_dt is fixed by a single shared prefactor multiplying 1/L. Child change: the slope of dL_dt versus 1/L is no longer constant along a trajectory but decays toward the saturation scale minimum_interface_mobility*interfacial_tension as mobility relaxes. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary trajectory, because the target derivative directly uses the evolving mobility state. The contrast is observable under the actual initial-condition contract by following one trajectory to later times with fixed initial L and fixed interfacial_tension: once mobility aging activates on a comparable timescale, late-time rates fall below any single-gain parent fit while remaining positive and curvature-driven.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set only provides one constant multiplier on 1/L. Refitting that gain can match either earlier or later portions of an aging trajectory, but not both when the same L-range is traversed with additional time-history-dependent suppression. Because the target equation itself uses the evolving mobility, this is not merely a change to an auxiliary trajectory; ignoring the mobility state removes the mechanism that generates the altered late-time asymptote.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes interface mobility is strictly constant, omitting physically admissible kinetic aging or defect-mediated drag relaxation that changes the coarsening rate over time even under fixed interfacial tension.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Interface mobility and interfacial tension are constant.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Time-dependent interface mobility due to evolving defect drag or structural relaxation during coarsening.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed interfacial_tension, dL_dt depends only on L through a single gain times 1/L. Proposed refinement: relax only the constancy of interface_mobility and make it an evolving state, leaving curvature-driven capillary motion intact. Varied condition: observation time within a trajectory, with initial condition and interfacial_tension held fixed. A single refitted parent prefactor cannot reproduce both early- and late-time rates across such conditions because it only multiplies the entire 1/L curve uniformly and cannot create time-history-dependent extra slowdown while preserving positivity, monotone decrease with L, and dissipative coarsening.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.interface_width: positive initial value; typically of order the initial diffuse interface thickness and smaller than or comparable to the early domain length
new_symbol_range_suggestions.interface_width_relaxation_time: positive; typically comparable to or shorter than the early coarsening time over which diffuse-interface corrections fade
new_symbol_range_suggestions.minimum_interface_width: positive or zero; typically not exceeding the initial interface_width

derivation_notes: The sharp-interface capillary drive interfacial_tension/L is replaced by a diffuse-interface form interfacial_tension/(L + interface_width), equivalent to weakening curvature driving when the domain size is not large compared with an evolving microscopic interfacial width. The new state is given a positive initial condition so the correction is active at early times rather than being trapped on the zero-effect invariant set interface_width = 0.
change_summary: The assumption of scale-independent capillary driving is relaxed by introducing a relaxing interfacial-width state that reduces the effective tension at small domain size. This produces a genuine crossover in the target mapping from suppressed early small-L coarsening to the parent inverse-length law at large L.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The curvature driving force uses a sharp-interface, scale-independent interfacial tension at all domain sizes.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite interface thickness during early coarsening renormalizes capillary stiffness so the effective curvature drive weakens when L is comparable to the diffuse interfacial scale.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When interface_width -> 0, or more generally interface_width/L -> 0 over the observed trajectory, the successor reduces to the parent law.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is dL_dt = interfacial_tension * interface_mobility / L, so at any observed interface_mobility the rate is a pure inverse-length law with fixed log-log slope -1 and no additional crossover in L.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the idealization of constant interfacial tension by allowing capillary stiffness to depend on domain scale through diffuse-interface corrections, so the effective driving force weakens at small L and approaches the parent law at large L; this bends the dL_dt versus L relation away from a strict 1/L form.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that span small to moderate domain sizes while mobility aging is held fixed or measured, the coarsening rate is suppressed more strongly at early small-L times than predicted by a single inverse-length law, then crosses over toward the parent behavior at larger L.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the characteristic domain size is only a few interface widths or other microscopic capillary lengths, so thin-interface asymptotics are not yet fully reached; the effect fades for L much larger than that microscopic scale.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, trajectories with early-time small L show stronger-than-parent deceleration even after accounting for the observed mobility relaxation; in holdout, later-time larger-L data approach the inverse-length parent scaling, extending the same crossover rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the sharp-interface limit where the microscopic capillary length becomes negligible compared with L, the effective tension tends to the constant interfacial_tension and the parent law is recovered.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A scale-dependent capillary correction requires one additional dynamical quantity representing the relaxing interfacial width or related microscopic structural scale; existing states L and interface_mobility alone cannot encode a transient length-dependent departure from strict 1/L once mobility is observed.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Diffuse-interface capillary correction to curvature-driven coarsening
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite interface thickness or capillary-stiffness renormalization during early coarsening makes the effective interfacial tension seen by curvature-driven motion depend on the evolving microstructural scale, producing a crossover from suppressed small-domain kinetics to the standard Allen-Cahn form.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding changes the target response law itself by making the coefficient of curvature-driven motion depend on a dynamical microscopic scale, creating an L-dependent crossover that cannot be produced by any constant gain retuning of interfacial_tension or mobility-aging parameters.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Interface mobility and interfacial tension are constant.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective capillary driving coefficient is reduced by a relaxing diffuse-interface width when domains are microscopically small.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When interface_width -> 0, or when L >> interface_width throughout the observed interval, the child collapses to interface_mobility * interfacial_tension / L.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent's single inverse-length curve at fixed observed interface_mobility, the child predicts lower dL_dt for small L with a smooth crossover toward the same large-L asymptote; this is observable when trajectories sample L comparable to interface_width and disappears once L greatly exceeds that scale.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set only rescales interface_mobility * interfacial_tension / L and therefore preserves the same 1/L dependence at all L. It cannot simultaneously fit suppressed early-time small-L rates and recovered later-time large-L inverse-length behavior across trajectories when interface_mobility is already part of the observed state evolution.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when the characteristic domain size is only a few interface widths or other microscopic capillary lengths, so thin-interface asymptotics are not yet fully reached; the effect fades for L much larger than that microscopic scale.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, trajectories with early-time small L show stronger-than-parent deceleration even after accounting for the observed mobility relaxation; in holdout, later-time larger-L data approach the inverse-length parent scaling, extending the same crossover rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the sharp-interface limit where the microscopic capillary length becomes negligible compared with L, the effective tension tends to the constant interfacial_tension and the parent law is recovered.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A scale-dependent capillary correction requires one additional dynamical quantity representing the relaxing interfacial width or related microscopic structural scale; existing states L and interface_mobility alone cannot encode a transient length-dependent departure from strict 1/L once mobility is observed.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the interfacial driving force is exactly sharp-interface and scale independent at all domain sizes, omitting early-stage diffuse-interface corrections that reduce curvature driving when domains are still microscopically small.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Interface mobility and interfacial tension are constant.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite interface thickness or capillary-stiffness renormalization during early coarsening makes the effective interfacial tension seen by curvature-driven motion depend on the evolving microstructural scale, producing a crossover from suppressed small-domain kinetics to the standard Allen-Cahn form.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: once interface_mobility is specified, dL_dt depends on L only through a single inverse factor, so all trajectories collapse onto the same 1/L shape up to gain changes from mobility aging. A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that the capillary driving force is scale independent from the very start of coarsening. In diffuse-interface systems, very small domains do not obey the sharp-interface curvature law exactly; the effective capillary force is weaker until the domain size becomes large compared with the interfacial width or another microscopic capillary scale. Vary the observed domain size along a trajectory, with interfacial_tension as the large-scale limit and mobility aging still present. The child then predicts a bent dL_dt(L) relationship: at small L the rate is lower than interface_mobility*interfacial_tension/L, while at larger L it crosses back toward that form. This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because even if interface_mobility is observed the mapping from L to dL_dt is no longer a single inverse law. The contrast is admissible when early coarsening explores L comparable to a microscopic interfacial scale; if all sampled L are already asymptotically large, the refinement becomes weak and the parent may suffice. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the suppressed early-time small-L rates and the recovered large-L inverse-length behavior across those conditions, because changing only constant interfacial_tension or mobility parameters rescales the whole curve without introducing the needed crossover in L.
